issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() as a no-argument method returning an int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This parameterized signature contradicts the specified design and would confuse students about the expected method signature and how to implement or call it (e.g., getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents() in the specification would expect to call a no-arg method).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getTotalNumberOfStudents method signature consistent with the problem statement (i.e., public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() with no parameters). If conditional inclusion of guest students is desired, provide an overload or a separate method (e.g., getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) in addition to the no-arg method) and update the template and documentation accordingly. Ensure getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents() and other usages call the no-arg method or the agreed-upon variant.

issues.description: The Problem Statement and UML specify a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, but the Solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This introduces an API/name-signature mismatch: students expect to implement/see a no-arg method named getTotalNumberOfStudents, while the solution exposes a parameterized variant. The difference in method signature (addition of boolean parameter named includeGuests) creates confusion mapping the requirement to the implementation and will prevent direct correspondence with tests or instructions that call the no-arg method.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the Problem Statement by providing a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns the total number of students (inscribed + guest). Either remove the boolean parameter from the existing method or add a no-arg overload: public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() { return numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents; } (optionally keep the parameterized variant but ensure the no-arg method exists and delegates to it).
